samples.summary: `seg()` is defined twice — private in `http-client.ts` and exported from `dry-run.ts` — so the "preview equals request" invariant this change is built on rests on two independent copies staying identical.
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:32` declares `function seg(value: string)`; `packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:12` exports an identical `seg()` that every command module imports (e.g. `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:4`, `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:6`). Changing the encoding policy in one (e.g. to permit `:` in a cell ref) silently makes every dry-run preview diverge from the URL actually fetched. Fix belongs on the new code: have `http-client.ts` import `seg` from `dry-run.ts` (or move it to a shared url module both import).

samples.summary: `apiKeysUrl()` re-implements HttpClient's api-key URL (host, route prefix and encoding) rather than deriving it, so the preview drifts silently if the route moves.
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:16-17` builds `${server}/workspaces/${seg(config.workspace)}/api-keys[/${seg(keyId)}]`; the real requests are built independently at `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:399`, `:406` and `:417`. Nothing ties the two together — no test asserts they agree — so moving the management route (e.g. under `/api/v1`) leaves `api-keys create|list|revoke --dry-run` printing a URL that is no longer the one sent. Exposing a URL builder on `HttpClient` and calling it from both sites would remove the duplication.

samples.summary: Cell/range endpoint selection and query encoding are duplicated in two command modules that mirror `HttpClient.getCells`/`getCell` by hand.
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:24-29` and `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:47-53` both re-derive `/documents/:d/tabs/:t/cells[?range=|/:ref]` that `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:358-369` owns. A change to the client's range handling (e.g. sending `range` as a path segment or adding a default) would not reach either preview, breaking the property the whole change asserts. Consider having the client expose the built path so both previews consume it.

samples.summary: The user-facing CLI reference in packages/documentation was not updated for the new read-command dry-run behaviour, while docs/design/cli.md was.
samples.evidence: `packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:111` documents `--dry-run` only as "Show request without executing" and its per-namespace sections mention dry-run solely for `docs import`, `sheets import` and `slides import` (lines 250-265, 331-335, 470-474); its `api-keys` section (line 549+) shows `create`/`list`/`revoke` with no note that they now preview instead of executing. `docs/design/cli.md:822-856` was updated with the full per-command notes, so the two consumer-facing docs now disagree.
searchedFor: grep 'dry' in packages/documentation/developers/cli.md (9 hits, all pre-existing write/import cases)

samples.summary: The transport-agnostic import runners now import from the `client/` layer just to reuse `seg()`, coupling modules whose stated design is to take an injected minimal HTTP surface.
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:6`, `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:5` and `packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:14` add `import { seg } from '../client/dry-run.js'`, although each file's header comment describes it as needing only a "Minimal HTTP surface … from the CLI's HttpClient" injected by the caller. No arch lint covers packages/cli (only frontend/backend `lint:arch` run), so nothing mechanical will flag this; a shared `util/` encoder would keep the layering intact.
